recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 501
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt shares a humorous 'Robophobia Equality Policy' written with ChatGPT's help, designed to encourage users to treat their AI support bot (named Bruce) with basic courtesy. The policy is tongue-in-cheek but serves a real purpose: the team lacks capacity to handle all support requests manually and relies on the bot as the frontline. It humorously prohibits 'robophobic' behavior like demanding a human simply because the bot lacks a childhood or a favorite sandwich, while still allowing legitimate criticism of AI responses.

recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 500
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt reflects on reaching his 500th weekly update video, sharing personal thoughts on the unconventional lifestyle he and Charlotte have built — one without clear work-life boundaries but full of purpose, meaning, and adventure. He addresses the audience question 'are you happy?' with candid reflection on the trade-offs of their chosen path.

recent_posts.title: Using agentic AI with Have I Been Pwned APIs via MCP
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt demonstrates how agentic AI can interact with Have I Been Pwned's APIs via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Using OpenClaw as an AI agent connected through a Telegram bot, he shows practical security use cases: identifying which employees appeared in a specific breach, analyzing stealer log data for corporate email addresses, discovering which external services employees are using with corporate credentials, and setting up background monitoring tasks that proactively alert on new breaches. The post also outlines HIBP's roadmap for deeper integration with mainstream AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT via OAuth, making breach data more accessible to non-technical users.

recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 499
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt shares an insight about Bruce, his AI assistant for handling support tickets. Rather than fully autonomous responses, the real value comes from a hybrid approach: Bruce auto-replies to straightforward tickets while requiring minimal human input for more complex ones. With just a small amount of context provided by a human, Bruce can construct high-quality replies and fully own the ticket resolution.

recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 498
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt shares frustrations with a delinquent enterprise customer whose invoices were 6+ months overdue despite 30-day payment terms, with the CEO responding poorly to his complaints. In response, he built a Xero integration (with Copilot's help) to automatically suspend HIBP enterprise services when invoices go unpaid, serving as both a practical solution and a public warning to slow-paying customers.

recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 497
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt shares how his team at Have I Been Pwned is increasingly offloading work to AI agents. They use a custom agent called OpenClaw (with a personal bot called PwnedClaw) to catalogue and process data breaches, GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio for development, and a Telegram bot called Pwny to crawl content and identify inconsistencies. Over two weeks, $854 was spent on Claude API tokens, which Hunt frames as cost-effective compared to human labor. The team is still early in exploring the potential of AI-assisted workflows.

recent_posts.title: HIBP Mega Update: Passkeys, k-Anonymity Searches, Massive Speed Enhancements and a Bulk Domain Verification API
recent_posts.summary: Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) is launching a major update with several new features and plan restructuring. Key additions include: k-anonymity searches for email addresses (similar to the existing Pwned Passwords approach), two new automated domain verification APIs (via DNS and email), auto-verification of subdomains for apex domain owners, passkey support for dashboard login, and a significant API performance improvement (~40% reduction in time-to-first-byte) by making rate limit checks asynchronous via Cloudflare Workers. Plans are being reorganized into Core, Pro, High RPM, and Enterprise tiers. MSPs can now use HIBP to monitor customers' domains under Pro and High RPM plans. Existing subscribers are protected from pricing changes until at least August 2025, with renewals potentially as late as August 2027.

recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 496
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt shares brief thoughts on OpenClaw, an agentic AI tool he's been experimenting with. He compares its current state to early aviation — rough but full of potential. While acknowledging much of the hype around it is overblown, he notes he's found genuinely useful applications for his own work and plans to dedicate a future video specifically to those use cases.

recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 493
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt's weekly update covers the Odido data breach, where multiple sequential data dumps were released over several days, dominating news in the Netherlands. The leak cadence appeared strategically timed for maximum media impact. While the extortionist likely gained no financial benefit, the incident sets a visible precedent and likely attracted significant law enforcement attention.

recent_posts.title: Weekly Update 492
recent_posts.summary: Troy Hunt's weekly update discusses the persistent gap between data breaches occurring and victims being notified. Companies facing breaches are caught in a lose-lose situation: paying ransoms funds criminals while not eliminating regulatory disclosure obligations, disclosing early exposes them to class-action lawsuits, and attempting to conceal breaches risks regulatory and customer backlash. The problem shows no signs of improving.

top_posts.title: Have I Been Pwned 2.0 is Now Live!
top_posts.summary: The revamped Have I Been Pwned website has been launched, introducing new features, improved search functionality, and a dedicated breach page with targeted advice. Email verification is enhanced, domain search is refined, and a new central dashboard consolidates user features. The site maintains the same API while adopting modern web technologies for better performance. A merch store is also available as part of the new offerings.

top_posts.title: Why Does Have I Been Pwned Contain "Fake" Email Addresses?
top_posts.summary: Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) contains seemingly "fake" email addresses because it extracts any string matching valid email format (alias@domain.tld) from breach data, without verifying if actual mailboxes exist behind them. These addresses appear in breaches because websites often store unverified email addresses in their databases before users complete email verification. The service processes 7 billion unique addresses, making individual mailbox verification impossible. The extraction logic is open source and follows RFC standards for email structure, not deliverability.

top_posts.title: Why data breach services must protect privacy regardless of moral judgments
top_posts.summary: Privacy is a fundamental human right that applies universally, regardless of personal moral judgments about individuals' activities. Using the Ashley Madison breach as a case study, the article examines why certain data breaches should be flagged as sensitive in Have I Been Pwned (HIBP). Email addresses in breaches don't always indicate what they seem—people join services for various reasons, accounts can be created without consent, and public doxing can have life-threatening consequences. Legally defined sensitive personal information includes data revealing racial origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, and health data. HIBP flags breaches as sensitive to prevent the service from being weaponized for public shaming, while still forwarding illegal content to law enforcement. The decision protects both individual privacy rights and the service's ability to operate.

top_posts.title: Welcoming CERN to Have I Been Pwned
top_posts.summary: CERN, the birthplace of the World Wide Web and home to the Large Hadron Collider, has joined Have I Been Pwned as the 41st intergovernmental organization. This partnership provides CERN with free access to query breach data across all their domains, helping protect their staff from online threats. The announcement highlights CERN's unique position as an intergovernmental organization that transcends national borders while facing the same cybersecurity challenges as sovereign governments.

top_posts.title: 'Pwned' Book Now Available for Free Download
top_posts.summary: Nearly four years ago, the author collaborated with Charlotte and Rob to write a book titled 'Pwned', detailing personal stories and behind-the-scenes insights related to the author's significant blog posts. Writing the book was a cathartic experience during a unique time when travel was limited. This week marks the 11th anniversary of 'Have I Been Pwned'. To celebrate, the author offers the book for free, with no strings attached, reflecting on the milestones and life changes since its launch.
